newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Dec 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Criticism of Wallaby coach Greg Smith has come to light in a recent interview with an anonymous Wallaby while on tour in Europe. While there is full support for the coaching techniques that have led to an unbeaten tour, communication problems have been revealed. Page 28.

Saintly-trainer Bart Cummings was relieved when the horse arrived back in Australian fit and well after its illness in Japan. Cummings immediately declared plans to race Saintly in the Australian Cup at Flemington in March were on hold until the horse's condition and progress could be further monitored. Page 28.

Opening batsman Michael Slater has been given a chance after being dropped before the first Test, with his inclusion in the Australian A side. He will play on the side with four recent Test players, captained by Steve Waugh. Page 30.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In response to concerns that local players were at a disadvantage, new Soceroo coach Terry Venables has assured Australian-based players will have first shot at a place in the World Cup campaign. Overseas-based players will not be considered for next month's four-nation tournament. Page 47.
Australian tennis-player Jason Stoltenberg picked up a A$125,000 pay cheque, despite being beaten by world number six Boris Becker on Tuesday in the A$7.4 million Grand Slam Cup. Page 48.

Jockey Glen Boss calmly accepted a $300 fine for misconduct over an incident with a punter, before exploding when questioned about his riding before the mishap. The inquiry was postponed to give Boss some cooling-off time. Page 48.
THE AGE

A project being driven by a coalition of surf industry moguls, Surfing Australia and the local Surf Coast Shire will lead to the likely establishment of a surf institute in Torquay. Specialist coaching and participation on the various competition circuit will be a focus, with equal weight also being placed on academic components. Page B6.

Cricketer Matthew Elliott is unlikely to play in the fourth Test in Adelaide, as he begins an expected two months of rehabilitation from knee surgery. The unlikelihood of playing in the fourth, or even the fifth, Test will make it difficult for Elliott to be picked on the ensuing tour of South Africa. Page B8.

The Australian Rugby League is expected to approve a Melbourne-based team in 1998, following a visit to Melbourne by two ARL officials to inspect Olympic Park and meet potential sponsors. While Super League has also expressed an interest in a Melbourne tam, there are doubts the city could support two. Page B8. --
THE HERALD SUN

Rugby Union legend David Campese will play for the last time in the Wallabies' Saturday match against the Barbarians in Twickenham. Acting Wallabies' captain Tim Horan believes the team will badly miss Campese, fondly farewelled from Test rugby at Cardiff Arms Park on Sunday. Page 90.

The Australian Baseball League appeals board is expected to hand down its decision on the appeal made by the Melbourne Reds against the ruling that made former player Greg Jelks a free agent. Page 93.

Australian golfer Ian Baker-Finch is set to make his comeback to tournament playing in Melbourne early in the new year. While Finch is pushing for the Victorian Open next month, his coach Steven Bann is turning his sights to a more realistic goal in the Australian Masters held in mid-February. Page 94.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The training of young Olympic rowers is being hindered by the rampant growth of aquatic plants in a three kilometre stretch of the Nepean River. Local experts have warned the nearby Olympic rowing course is also in danger of being overrun by the plants. Page 21.

The gap left by the retirement of legendary footballer Terry Lamb could well be filled by Duncan McCrae after his signing to Canterbury for next season. The club is looking for a halfback to replace Lamb and should McCrae produce the form, he will be given the spot in first grade. Page 88.

Junior batsman Sally Butler has finished her schoolgirl cricket career by helping her team to an outright win, scoring 125 runs in under three hours. Butler, a five-time New South Wales student representative, is regarded as a future Test player. Page 9.
